REASON FOR VISIT: New patient consultation for biopsy-proven lung adenocarcinoma, right upper lobe.
DIAGNOSIS: Stage IIIA non-small cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC), EGFR exon 19 deletion positive.

HISTORY: Mr. James Holloway is a 58-year-old never-smoker presenting with a 3-month history of
progressive dyspnea and 15-lb weight loss. CT chest showed a 4.2 cm RUL mass with ipsilateral
mediastinal lymphadenopathy. Brain MRI negative. Biopsy confirmed lung adenocarcinoma.
Molecular testing: EGFR exon 19 deletion. ALK/ROS1 negative. PD-L1 TPS 5%.

TREATMENT PLAN: Given EGFR exon 19 deletion, plan to initiate erlotinib (Tarceva) 150mg daily.
Discussed mechanism of EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibition. Common side effects including acneiform
rash, diarrhea, paronychia reviewed. Patient counseled on photosensitivity. Will monitor LFTs.
HOLD chemotherapy at this time — EGFR-directed therapy preferred over platinum doublet.

ASSESSMENT: EGFR-mutant NSCLC, good performance status (ECOG 1). Favorable prognosis expected
with targeted therapy. Patient and family agreeable with treatment plan. Return in 3 weeks.

Note Dept: Oncology

FOLLOW-UP: 7 months on erlotinib. 
CT CHEST (2021-09-28): New 1.8cm subpleural nodule right lower lobe. Primary tumor stable. 
Concern for emerging resistance. Recommend liquid biopsy / repeat tissue biopsy.

MOLECULAR TESTING: Plasma ctDNA — EGFR T790M mutation detected (allele fraction 0.8%).
ASSESSMENT: Acquired resistance to erlotinib, T790M-mediated. Patient progressed on erlotinib.

PLAN: Transition to osimertinib (Tagrisso) 80mg daily — third-generation EGFR TKI with T790M 
activity and CNS penetration. Discontinue erlotinib. Counseled on side effects: QTc prolongation,
cardiomyopathy, interstitial lung disease (rare but serious). Baseline EKG obtained — normal QTc.
Echocardiogram ordered. Follow-up in 4 weeks.

PLAN: Continue osimertinib 80mg daily. Next CT in 4 months. CBC, CMP, LFTs within normal limits.

Patient aware of prognosis — maintained excellent outlook, engaged family present.

CONSULTATION: Newly diagnosed metastatic breast cancer.

PATIENT: Ms. Linda Kowalski, 62F. History of ER+/PR+/HER2- right breast cancer treated with
lumpectomy + radiation + adjuvant anastrozole in 2014. Now presents with new bone pain x6 weeks.

WORKUP:
- CT chest/abdomen/pelvis: Multiple lytic bone lesions (vertebral bodies T7, L2, L4, right iliac),
  no visceral metastases. No liver or lung involvement.
- Bone scan: Diffuse osseous uptake consistent with widespread bone metastases.  
- Biopsy of right iliac lesion: ER 95%/PR 60%/HER2 IHC 1+ (FISH non-amplified). Ki-67 18%.
- Repeat ER/PR/HER2 consistent with primary. No change in receptor status.
- ESR1 mutation: Not detected on liquid biopsy.

ASSESSMENT: HR+/HER2- metastatic breast cancer (MBC), bone-only disease, de novo metastatic 
(recurrence >4 years from adjuvant AI). Favorable biology, no visceral crisis.

TREATMENT PLAN:
First-line therapy: Palbociclib (Ibrance) 125mg daily x21 days/28-day cycle + letrozole 2.5mg daily.
Rationale: PALOMA-2 data supports palbociclib + letrozole as standard first-line for HR+/HER2- MBC.
Bone support: Zoledronic acid (Zometa) 4mg IV q4 weeks — dental clearance required first.
Ovarian function: Post-menopausal confirmed (FSH/LH elevated).

Side effects discussed: neutropenia (most common — grade 3/4 in ~66% of patients but rarely febrile),
fatigue, alopecia (rare), nausea. CBC monitoring required weeks 2 of cycle 1, then before each cycle.
Patient motivated and understands treatment plan. Return in 4 weeks.
